studies.Screening Record ID: 36601047|Non-nutritive sweetener intake|Kidney and renal pelvis cancer
studies.Population: Postmenopausal women enrolled in the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study (WHI-OS)
studies.Ethnicity Basis: Default: no protocol-mapped specific country or population was established
studies.Reference: Association of Artificially Sweetened Beverage Consumption and Urinary Tract Cancers in the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study.
studies.Authors: Ringel NE, Hovey KM, Andrews CA, Mossavar-Rahmani Y, Shadyab AH, Snetselaar LG, Howard BV, Iglesia CB
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The question regarding ASBs was as follows: “During the past 3 mo, how often did you drink these beverages?” (Beverages refer to “diet drinks such as Diet Coke or diet fruit drinks,” with a 12 fl. oz. can as a reference serving size.)

sample_size.excerpt: In this secondary analysis of the Women’s Health Initiative Observational Study that included 80 388 postmenopausal women, higher consumption of artificially sweetened beverages was associated with a higher risk of kidney cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: 2 C) relative to rare consumption, and this risk persisted after adjustments (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03–1.75). A similar increased risk was seen with ASB consumption of one or more servings per day ( Fig.

confidence_interval.excerpt: 2 C) relative to rare consumption, and this risk persisted after adjustments (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03–1.75).

comparison.excerpt: The frequency of artificially sweetened beverage consumption was categorized as follows: rare artificially sweetened beverage consumption (never to fewer than one serving per week), frequent consumption (one to six servings per week), and daily consumption (more than one servings per day).

design.excerpt: This was a secondary analysis of data from the Women’s Health Initiative Observational Study, a multicenter longitudinal prospective study of the health of 93 676 postmenopausal women with a mean follow-up time of 13.5 yr.

timing.excerpt: The WHI-OS is a prospective, multicenter cohort study of 93 676 postmenopausal women.

continent.excerpt: Women were identified at 40 clinical centers across the USA and enrolled from 1993 to 1998.
